Hot girl summer
HOT gurl SUM-er
noun phrase (Gen-Z slang)
Popularized by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, whose fans were "Hotties"; she used the phrase from 2018 and released the single "Hot Girl Summer" in August 2019, filing to trademark it the same year. She described it as being unapologetically yourself and having a good time; in common use it means a season of confident, carefree, flirtatious living without commitments. Later echoes: "hot girl walk," "brat summer."

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang a hot girl summer is a season of carefree confidence: going out, looking good, saying yes to fun, and keeping things casual with men. The originator framed it as being yourself and enjoying life; the song and the culture made clear what "having fun" included. The Christian observation: Scripture is for joy and for confidence, but not this kind. The hot girl summer is built on the premise that a woman’s body and evenings are her own to spend as she likes. Paul answers with the most freeing sentence a young woman can hear: "know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price" (1Co 6:19–20). "Flee fornication" (1Co 6:18); "this is the will of God, even your sanctification" (1Th 4:3). Paul’s summer plan is the opposite: "walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness" (Rom 13:13). The older women of Titus 2 are told to teach the younger "to be discreet, chaste" (Tit 2:5) — not dull, but guarded, because what they are guarding is precious. A father tells his daughter: you can have a joyful summer — sun, friends, laughter, adventure — without spending yourself; the girl who is not her own is the freest girl at the party.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (Megan Thee Stallion, 2019) for a season of carefree, confident, uncommitted fun — a promise of freedom that Scripture answers: ye are not your own, ye are bought with a price.

HOT GIRL SUMMER, n. phr. (Gen-Z slang, 2019–present; from Megan Thee Stallion) A season of confident, carefree, social, and often flirtatious living, free of commitments. "No boyfriend, no drama, hot girl summer."

Originator’s gloss: being unapologetically yourself and having a good time.

Variants: hot girl walk, hot girl era; later brat summer (2024).

Webster (1828), root word summer: “SUM'MER, noun With us, the season of the year comprehended in the months June, July and August; during which time, the sun being north of the equator, shines more directly upon this part of the earth, which, together with the increased length of the days, renders this the hottest period of the year.”

Decode for parents: the phrase sells your daughter freedom from commitment. Offer her the better freedom of belonging to Christ.

Key Scripture

1Co 6:19 — "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?"

1Co 6:20 — "For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's."

1Co 6:18 — "Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body."

Rom 13:13 — "Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying."

Tit 2:5 — "To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed."

Modern Corruption

Hot girl summer sells young women a season of self-ownership and casual romance as freedom; Scripture names it wantonness and offers the true freedom of a body bought with a price.

expand to see more

The phrase is a sales pitch with a season attached. It promises confidence, fun, and freedom, and defines freedom as having no one to answer to — no commitments, no limits, no one’s girl. Paul had a list for that kind of summer: "rioting and drunkenness... chambering and wantonness" (Rom 13:13). It leaves young women used, not free, and the men who cheer it on are the ones who benefit.

The gospel is the stronger confidence. "Ye are not your own... ye are bought with a price" (1Co 6:19–20) sounds like a restriction until you realize it means you are worth the blood of Christ. A daughter who knows that can enjoy every good thing of summer and still walk "honestly, as in the day." Let the older women in her life teach her what Titus 2 calls discretion: not dullness, but the guarding of something precious.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Megan Thee Stallion’s "Hotties" → 2018–2019 "hot girl summer" (single, trademark) → general slang for a carefree, uncommitted season → spin-offs.
